# jj performance

<!-- Generated by scripts/jj-e2e/render-performance.py; edit the JSON inputs. -->

Compare jj on girt with stock jj at the same base revision. Lower ratios are better. Failures and
missing results sort first, followed by the worst measured ratio across sizes. These warm-cache
measurements describe the recorded build epochs below. Cells can use different girt revisions;
consult each row’s binary fingerprints and epoch.

🟢 ≤1.20×; 🟠 >1.20–2.00×; 🔴 >2.00×; ❌ failure/refusal; ⏳ pending. `n` is the number of
successful girt samples; JSON records each tool separately.

## Limits and interpretation

Historical rename-detection refusals are tracked in
[#227](https://github.com/joshka/girt/issues/227). Historical fetch/clone source pack-index refusals
are tracked in [#228](https://github.com/joshka/girt/issues/228). The historical new-bookmark push
destination refusal is tracked in [#234](https://github.com/joshka/girt/issues/234). Other
originally refused push variants failed in prerequisite fetch before timing. The table reports the
latest measured result for each cell; superseded refusals remain in the retained raw evidence. The
related empty/binary-file rename-candidate counting policy is tracked in
[#229](https://github.com/joshka/girt/issues/229); it is context, not a separately measured
slowdown.

A refusal during prerequisite setup has no timed girt sample. A timeout has a recorded limit and no
successful girt ratio. Neither is presented as a fast result. Stock jj taking more than twice Git is
flagged separately in the JSON as `jj_level_gap`. Git equivalents sometimes perform different work;
read each row’s workload notes. Git has no timed counterpart for colocated initialization (the input
is already a Git repository), import (Git already sees its own refs), or jj undo/operation restore
(Git has no equivalent repository-wide operation restoration). Reflogs approximate jj evolution and
operation history but contain different records. Ranges, peak RSS, sample counts, issue mappings,
and limitations are in [the results JSON](benchmarks/jj-matrix.json). Machine load was not
controlled; treat results as provisional where retained sample load or ranges show contention. Clean
GC measures backend policy as well as speed: the backends can choose different packing work when
nothing needs collection. Its ratio is not equal-work repack throughput.

## Provenance

- Measurement dates: 2026-10-14 through 2026-10-16 (America/Los_Angeles).
- Machine: Apple M2 Max; macOS-26.6.2-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O.
- girt: `d3a70f474397e992a33e712e3df8860ab3b94109`.
- jj adapter: `5f5fc486e1be57dd4e22c79f657be4ddc36e9006`.
- Stock jj base: `35dbc3623b6dd5a23daf5b5ca09b8640694a72ae`.
- Git: git version 2.56.0; release commit `a018953688f1b10bddf91bff8747068f5f4746a4`.
- Build: release; debug=1; strip=none; codegen-units=1; rustc 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28).

The Git commit identifies release source; distribution packaging may add patches. Binary
fingerprints and per-repository object, ref, tag, worktree, and pack facts are in
[the JSON provenance block](benchmarks/jj-matrix.json). Original small-run fingerprints are retained
separately from later binaries rebuilt from the identical source revisions. The original small-run
Git binary fingerprint was not captured. Empty per-row Git fingerprint lists mean no sample-local
capture; later Git identity is recorded at provenance level. Small new, rebase/10, and
status/many-edits profiles used the rebuilt frozen-source binary, not the original timing binary.
Older profile entries can lack a sample-local fingerprint; interpret them using their retained build
epoch. Profiles and raw checkpoints are retained locally at the evidence paths; they are not bundled
in this repository. The [original 53 small rows](jj-performance-original-small.json) retain the
historical timings; five cells are intentionally superseded by the fetch and limited-log
corrections. The corrected small cells use a same-HEAD repacked fixture; per-epoch layouts are in
the provenance JSON.

Formerly refused cells were remeasured against girt `24713e37e46ea09af76fb2379ee7b45214afc366` using
the same jj base plus mechanical API compatibility changes. The compatibility patch fingerprint and
rebuilt binary fingerprint are in the provenance JSON. Other cells retain their earlier builds; this
is a mixed-revision matrix, not a complete rerun of current girt main.

## Method

Build both binaries before taking the shared `/tmp/girt-timing.lock`. Prepare inputs outside the
lock. Use fresh APFS `cp -cR` copies for mutating samples, one large copy at a time; checkpoint
timing and validation before deleting it. Reuse clean read-only baselines and verify unchanged jj
operation heads. Later mutation inputs were rebuilt after history rendering accumulated internal Git
objects; subsequent read cells use separate baselines to preserve pristine mutation inputs.
Automatic Git maintenance is disabled in the later run epoch; explicit GC remains measured.

Linux has tracked paths differing only by case. On case-insensitive APFS, Git rebase setup verifies
that every unstaged path is such an alias and marks only those paths assume-unchanged before timing.
Other unstaged edits fail setup. This platform limitation means the checkout cannot represent both
versions of those files faithfully.

The original method takes six samples per tool in Git, girt, stock, stock, girt, Git blocks. The
remaining Linux cells use adaptive calibration in Git, stock, girt order: if the slowest first
sample exceeds 60 seconds, take one sample per tool; if it exceeds 10 seconds, take three; otherwise
take six. Further samples alternate girt and stock positions. Preserve completed older cells and
partial samples on resume. Slow-cell ratios therefore have lower precision. Counts in the JSON
describe the samples actually retained.

Kill each timed girt process group at `max(2 × first stock-jj seconds, 5 seconds)`. Stock jj and Git
each have a 600-second cap. Timeouts fail the cell and record the limit. Report medians, full
ranges, and peak RSS using `/usr/bin/time -l`. Release the lock between timed samples in
bounded-disk mode. Caches are warm and are not flushed.

Full `git fsck` succeeded for every small mutation variant on the frozen build. Clone and explicit
GC were fully checked at each size, and the current-build Linux clone was checked again. The
operation-type policy reuses earlier checks across build epochs: current-build fetch, push, and
untracked-status reruns did not receive new full fsck checks. This limits validation of those
reruns. Semantic checks cover imported/exported refs and actual garbage removal. Profiles diagnose
gaps without replacing timings; adaptive diagnostic recordings are capped at five seconds.

Fetch cells perform an untimed fetch before introducing the measured commit/tag delta. This imports
existing tags and makes noop a genuine second fetch with no remote changes. The final stale-push
rerun prepares remote-tracking refs with untimed Git fetch plus jj import, avoiding a repeated
native-fetch workload before the separately timed push. Earlier completed push cells retain their
original jj-fetch preparation. Limited log uses `::@ --limit 100` against Git `-n 100`; the
superseded `ancestors(@, 100)` selected up to 100 parent steps, not 100 output revisions. Affected
small/medium cells were remeasured; the corrected Linux limited log was also rerun. Linux girt fetch
warm-up was refused by the original build’s pack-index limit; later current-main reruns use the
fixes recorded in their build epoch. Superseded samples and fingerprints remain archived separately
from the corrected results.

## Refresh before a release

On a quiet macOS machine, build the intended frozen jj/girt revisions and prepare all fixtures under
`~/tmp/girt-bench` or `~/tmp/girt-fixtures`. Follow
[the matrix runner instructions](../scripts/jj-e2e/README.md), recording exact commits, binary
hashes, fixture facts, failures, and issue links. Keep the raw checkpoint and logs. Publication is a
manual normalization step: the runner emits a timing list and raw checkpoint, not this publication
schema. Merge selected reruns by repository/operation, retain replaced records, classify statuses,
attach reviewed issue/profile mappings, and audit sample counts, ranges, fingerprints, and
validation epochs before updating the publication envelope. Update the results and provenance in
`docs/benchmarks/jj-matrix.json` from that run, then regenerate and check the page:

```sh
python3 scripts/jj-e2e/render-performance.py
python3 scripts/jj-e2e/render-performance.py --check
```

CI runs only the freshness check. It never runs benchmarks.
